In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no significant correlation between supernova type and host galaxy type.
the host galaxies of SNe II and SNe Ibc are of similar Hubble type, whereas the host galaxies of SN 1999aa–like SNe Ib are of later Hubble types.
SNe Ibc occur preferentially in late‐type galaxies and SNe Ia in early‐type systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the distribution of SNe Ia over Hubble types is bimodal, with the two peaks occurring at E and Sbc.
the Hubble types of the hosts of the different subtypes of supernovae are not significantly different.
we have found that the host galaxies of SNe Ia, II, Ibc, and IIb are all different from one another.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Hubble sequence is not a sufficient predictor of supernova type.
the host galaxy type of a supernova has a profound effect on its classification and luminosity, and that this effect is different for different types of supernovae.
, while the host-galaxy properties of SNe Ia are well established, those of SNe II remain unclear.
